name: Pyxis
introduction: is the Mariner’s Compass, introduced by Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille in the 1750s next to the old ship Argo Navis. It is a faint line of three stars in the southern Milky Way.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Pyxis contains T Pyxidis, a recurrent nova. Every few decades, gas piled onto its white dwarf from a companion ignites, and the star brightens by thousands of times; its latest outburst came in 2011.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Alpha Pyxidis](hip:42828) is a hot blue giant about 800 light-years away. [Beta Pyxidis](hip:42515) and [Gamma Pyxidis](hip:43409) are yellow and orange giants.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: Pyxis lies at the edge of the Milky Way, where the Gum Nebula, a vast shell of gas from ancient supernovae, extends from neighboring Vela.
